legislature_how_congress:
[Delegates] The congress has {0} delegates, chosen tier by tier through lower congresses: each region gets delegates by population, shared among parties by organisational strength (membership); while parties are banned the leading party keeps two thirds.
[Term] A new congress every {1} years; a delegate who dies, leaves the country or changes party is replaced by the same party.
[Leadership] The leader of the leading party is head of state. There is no cabinet formation and no vote of no confidence. Parties in political consultation accept the leading party's leadership and take part in shaping the programme.
[Programme] The leading party pushes one constitutional clause at a time; it passes once enough votes are gathered in the congress.
legislature_how_presidential:
[Seats] The legislature has {0} seats; the number follows the order of magnitude of the population, and seats go to parties by vote (by region once universal suffrage is in force).
[Members] Each party nominates adult members, office holders first, then merit, then renown; seats without a candidate stay vacant.
[Term] Full elections every {1} years; a member who dies, leaves the country or changes party is replaced by the same party.
[President] After each general election the leader of the party that forms the government becomes president, head of both state and government, for a fixed term the legislature cannot cut short, within the constitutional term limit.
[Agenda] The president's party pushes one constitutional clause at a time; it passes once enough votes are gathered, otherwise it stalls at second reading.

court_how_body:
[Memorial] A faction spends {0} political capital to submit an issue it supports. Only it can raise its unique issues; public issues such as taxes, war and peace, and examinations any faction can raise.
[Agenda] Where there is an agenda-setter (the Qin-Han chancellor, the Tang Secretariat head, the Ming senior secretary, the chief elector, the leading senator), he decides whether to forward it; if his faction opposes it, it is buried unless the proposer is his ally or pays to lobby. A faction without a seat or a seated ally must petition from outside and may not be heard. An enfeoffment court has no agenda-setter.
[Debate] Every faction takes a side, weighted by its strength (half by council seats where there is a council); below {1}% in favour the memorial fails.
[Decision] The ruler approves, rejects or shelves it by support, favour, his own stance and temperament, and his court policy; a child or puppet ruler is replaced by the strongman or regent. Under Qin-Han the chancellor's stance sways the decision; under the Tang the Chancellery may veto once after the emperor signs.
[Enact] An approved memorial progresses month by month, faster the more of the council backs it; opponents can obstruct it.
[Struggle] Each year factions gain capital from offices and seats and spend it to impeach, obstruct, court favour, ally or recruit. Rejection and exclusion breed grievance: above 60% a faction boycotts the court, and at the extreme with no favour left it may take up arms.
[Exceptions] Claims to the throne, popular campaigns (lifting the party ban) and local pushes bypass the court.

institution_huaxia_three_departments_des: The chancellor's power is split three ways: the Secretariat drafts, the Chancellery reviews and may veto, and the Department of State Affairs carries out decisions through the six ministries of personnel, revenue, rites, war, justice and works. Once enacted, the central government changes from the Three Excellencies and Nine Ministers to the Three Departments: the Secretariat sets the agenda, the Chancellery may veto after the emperor signs, and State Affairs executes. Before it the court follows the Qin-Han model, where the chancellor runs the government and can check the emperor.
institution_huaxia_grand_secretariat_des: The Secretariat is abolished and Hanlin scholars advise in the Wenyuan Pavilion, growing into the Grand Secretariat: the senior secretary drafts and the emperor endorses in vermilion. Once enacted, the court gains a cabinet whose seats the emperor fills by ability, favour and court policy; the senior secretary drafts memorials, the secretaries' ability affects central corruption, and the Chancellery's veto disappears.

three_departments_body:
[Secretariat] Its head decides whether a memorial goes forward; if his faction opposes it, it is buried unless the proposer is his ally or pays to lobby.
[Chancellery] After the emperor signs, the Chancellery reviews: if its head's faction opposes, it may veto and send the memorial back, once per memorial.
[State Affairs] Approved memorials are carried out through the six ministries; the more department heads and ministers back it, the faster it goes.
In debate the department heads and ministers carry half the weight.

corps_rules_hint: Each corps equals eight old legions; men are drawn from city population, returned on demobilization and lost when killed. Monthly: realms split forces to defend threatened cities and concentrate the rest on one or two sectors; when attack (strength × organization × firepower) beats defence (×1.25 plus entrenchment, or town militia if undefended) the front advances zone by zone and a city falls once all its zones are taken; corps at zero organization rout. Each tank, plane or other vehicle adds 4% firepower to its realm's corps. Terrain of the tile being attacked matters: mountains, hills, forest, jungle, rivers, marsh and cities cut attack and limit how many tiles fall a month; jungle, marsh, desert and snow drain extra organization; mountains, marsh and jungle halve march speed. Solid mountain ranges (tiles three-quarters mountain or summit, impassable to ground units in the base game) are marched around and never attacked through; they fall with their city once the rest of it is taken.
zhou_rule_0: Royal Supremacy: the royal house is strong; vassals may not wage war on their own and follow the king's campaigns. Spring and Autumn begins when the royal army is weaker than the strongest vassal's, the mandate falls below 60 or the royal capital is lost (Bronze Casting must be known first; with Ironworking, a mandate below 70 is enough).
zhou_rule_1: Spring and Autumn: royal power declines, the king can no longer take land from vassals, and vassals pay the royal house only a token twentieth of their taxes; vassals may fight one another and taking a capital annexes that state; none may attack the royal domain, and whoever does is punished by the hegemon and the vassals; when barbarians attack a vassal, the king and the hegemon come to its aid; vassals pay the hegemon a tenth of their revenue each year, and the hegemon arbitrates wars and punishes states that withhold tribute or usurp the royal title. The Warring States begin when ministers partition a great state, annexation leaves seven vassals or fewer, or the mandate falls below 30 (Ironworking must be known first; with Steelmaking, a mandate below 40 or nine vassals or fewer is enough).
zhou_rule_2: Warring States: great states proclaim themselves kings and the hegemony ends; vassals no longer pay taxes to the royal house or follow the king to war, the king no longer sends aid, and the royal domain may be attacked; states reform (+25% wartime levies, a tenth more revenue, resentful old nobility); wars between vassals aim at annexation, kings and reformed states attack weaker neighbours, and lone one-city states may surrender outright; when one state dominates, the rest form a vertical alliance (each member answers a given war only four times in ten) and weak states may side with it. Whoever takes or is ceded the royal domain replaces the royal house; ruling half the realm's cities directly, or a third with no other state holding a third as many, makes it emperor and brings in commanderies and counties.
zhou_rule_3: Unified: the enfeoffment order has ended and the realm is governed by commanderies and counties.

pure_map_notice_text:
Pure Map Mode is on, so buildings, trees, plants and units are not drawn on the map — this is not a bug.

Buildings, population, rulers, officials and the economy all keep running; the map is drawn like a digital map instead: country colors, terrain, roads and city plans, with street-level labels when zoomed in.

To get the original visuals back, turn off "Pure Map Mode" in the mod settings and restart the game.

institution_huaxia_sacrifice_desc: Altars to Heaven, Earth and the ancestors, served by shaman-priests; every great matter is first put to the turtle shell. The ruler holds a yearly sacrifice: it costs treasury and grants +2 legitimacy, and the coming year is divined; if the treasury cannot pay, the rite lapses and legitimacy falls by 3. Before declaring war the ruler divines: an auspicious omen gives +1 legitimacy and all corps +10 organization, an ill omen -10 organization and -1 legitimacy.

institution_huaxia_slavery_desc: Captives, criminals and debtors are made slaves, hereditary bondsmen who till and build for the nobility. Taking a city carries off 12% of its people as slaves to the capital; criminals and debtors keep every city at least 4% slaves, and famine drives more to sell themselves. Slave labour yields one and a half times the output, which belongs to the slaveholders untaxed; slaves are never levied. A few buy or flee their freedom each year. Cities with slaves raise a slaveholder class. Slaves bear heavy grievances, and when they organize, they rise in a slave revolt.

guoren_riot_exile_history: The guoren rioted; {0} fled to {1}, and the guoren raised {2}.
institution_huaxia_guoye_desc: The capital is the guo, the countryside beyond is the ye. Commoners of the capital are guoren: they pay light taxes (80% of the rate), bear arms for the altars of the state, can all be levied, and have a voice in affairs of state. Commoners of the countryside are yeren: they pay heavy taxes (120% of the rate) and serve as labourers, only a quarter of them levied. Under a tyrannical, fatuous or dissolute ruler the guoren murmur; when their anger gathers they riot, the ruler flees, and the guoren raise the heir or a kinsman in his place. Discontented yeren rise in ordinary class revolts.
institution_huaxia_registered_households: The divide between guo and ye is abolished: all people are entered in one household register, given land by head count, taxed by household and levied by register. Replaces Guo and Ye: within a year guoren and yeren all become peasants with equal taxes and service; the guoren lose their privileges and grumble.
institution_huaxia_abolish_slavery_desc: Slaves are freed as commoners, registered and given land to till; the sale of persons and bondage are forbidden. Replaces Slavery: within a year every slave becomes a commoner and slaveholders become landlords (or nobles where land cannot be bought). Slave labour output and the enslavement of captives end. Slaveholders and nobles bitterly oppose it, and the reform readily provokes revolt.

institution_ideology_eunuchs_desc: Palace servants bound to the ruler; normally with the Emperor's Faction, but under a weak ruler favoured eunuchs split off and seize power. Court only.
institution_ideology_consort_kin_desc: The empress's family, ennobled by marriage to the throne, meddling in government through the inner palace. Court only; the Empress's Party at court.
institution_ideology_great_clans_desc: Great families with generations of office, birth and privilege, sharing rule with the throne. Found in every culture, held by nobles and slaveholders; the Clans at court.
institution_ideology_imperial_power_desc: Exalt the ruler and humble the ministers; supreme imperial authority, curbing the fiefs and centralizing power. Found in every culture, held by officials; the Emperor's Party at court.
institution_ideology_yin_yang_desc: The five phases and the heavens, the resonance of Heaven and man and the cycle of the five virtues, held by shamans and diviners. Branches off from shamanic rites once the culture has ritual rites; favoured by peasants.
institution_ideology_diplomatists_desc: Vertical and horizontal alliances, persuading the lords, deciding fates by eloquence, and trade between states. Favoured by merchants and wandering scholars; appears with writing and currency.
institution_ideology_strategists_desc: The art of war and stratagem, military merit and preparedness, war to end war. Favoured by soldiers; appears with writing and military registers.
institution_ideology_agrarianism_desc: Ruler and people tilling side by side, agriculture as the root, stable prices. Favoured by peasants and yeren; appears with writing and census.
institution_ideology_mohism_desc: Universal love and opposition to aggressive war, promotion of the worthy, frugality, and skilled craft and machines. Favoured by artisans and guoren; appears with writing and masonry.
institution_ideology_huang_lao_desc: Quietude and non-action: let the people rest, keep taxes and corvée light, do not disturb them. Favoured by peasants and guoren; appears with writing.
institution_ideology_legalism_desc: Law as the only teaching and officials as the only teachers; agriculture and war, clear rewards and punishments, a strong centre and an absolute ruler. Favoured by officials and soldiers; appears with writing and law codes.
institution_ideology_confucianism_desc: Rites, benevolence and righteousness; rule by virtue and moral teaching, and the proper order of ruler and subject, father and son. Favoured by officials and landlords; appears once the culture has writing and ritual rites.
institution_ideology_animism_desc: All things have spirits: reverence for mountains, rivers, beasts, ancestral spirits and magic. Held by everyone before the culture has writing; afterwards it branches into the culture's own schools and faiths.

institution_huaxia_nine_rank_desc: Impartial and Just officers in each province rate local men in nine ranks for appointment, and rank follows pedigree. Great-clan sons enter office far more easily (about three vacancies in four go to them, against two in five under recommendation), and pedigree hardens, declining only half as fast; no humble family reaches the top ranks, no great clan sinks to the bottom. Replaced by the civil examinations.

assign_settlement_description: Click a settlement, then a city: the settlement and its surrounding area move to that city, whether or not they border (it becomes an exclave otherwise) and even if enemies hold it (the occupation record is cleared). A city's seat and urban core never move with a settlement.
raze_settlement_description: Click a village or town: an intact one is razed to ruins (half its people flee; it may be rebuilt in peaceful years). Click the ruins again to erase them for good; the countryside will not rebuild there. Click a factory district to demolish it.
place_town_description: Click land to found a town. Ownership, land claims and freedom from limits work as for villages; trails connect along the terrain. Nomad camp cities found yurt towns; open a town to change its style, trade or make it a walled town.
place_village_description: Click land to found a village; hills, woods and dry land all work, however close to other settlements or factories. On a city's land it belongs to that city; on unclaimed land it goes to the nearest adjacent city (or the nearest city anywhere), with that area claimed. Trails connect along the terrain. Nomad camp cities found yurt villages anywhere; open a village to change its style, trade or tier. Not on water, lava, mountains, walls or inside a city's urban core.
empirecraft_law_fixed_settlements_descri: When on, the AI no longer founds villages or towns, war no longer burns them, and ruins are not rebuilt by themselves; settlements are added, upgraded, razed and rebuilt only by hand (Found Village, Found Town, Raze, and the small window opened by clicking a settlement). Use it to lay out a historical map: dense settlements mean dense population.
settlement_window_fixed_off: The world law "Fixed settlements" makes villages and towns change only by hand
settlement_window_fixed_on: Fixed settlements is on: villages and towns change only by hand
settlement_window_assign_hint: To hand it to another city: use Reassign on the building tab

factory_large_description: Click land to place a large factory district (8×8, six factories), randomly fitted from all eight factory types regardless of technology or docks or nearby settlements; unclaimed land goes to the nearest city. Open the district to rename, expand, add or remove factories (any type) and change levels.
factory_medium_description: Click land to place a medium factory district (6×6, four factories), randomly fitted from all eight factory types regardless of technology or docks or nearby settlements; unclaimed land goes to the nearest city. Open the district to rename, expand, add or remove factories (any type) and change levels.
factory_small_description: Click land to place a small factory district (4×4, two factories), randomly fitted from all eight factory types regardless of technology or docks or nearby settlements; unclaimed land goes to the nearest city. place_fort_description: Click land to build a fort: walls and a garrison, no residents. Click on or within five tiles of a wall to build it into the wall as a gate (walls on mountains and passes too): the wall joins the fort on both sides, roads cross the wall through it, and its holder, friends and allies pass the wall there unhindered. When enemies attack its area, defenders fight 30% (outpost), 60% (fort) or 90% (great fort) stronger; halved against heavy cannon. Click it to upgrade.

build_palace_description: Click a city to build a palace: the first click only warns, click again within five seconds to build. In an empire's core realm it is the imperial palace — the empire core's default capital, moved there at once; one per empire, the old one is removed. In any other realm it is a royal palace — the city becomes the realm's capital, and the palace stays whatever the city's size.
place_city_description: Click a realm's land to select it, then click its land or unclaimed land to found a new city there, named and cultured after that realm; clicking another realm's land switches the selection. Without a selection, unclaimed land goes to the adjacent realm with the nearest capital (or the nearest realm anywhere). A tenth of the population moves in from the realm's nearest city. Distance to other cities or factories does not matter, hills are fine; not on water, lava, mountains, walls or another city's seat.

institution_youmu_steppe_clans_desc: Herders follow water and grass, each clan under its own chief, wealth counted in livestock. Wars between tribes are raids for herds and goods that end in reparations; no tribe can absorb another.
institution_youmu_clan_union_desc: Once enacted, a tribe that wins a war makes the loser acknowledge it as leader (before this, wars end only in reparations), and the winner becomes a tribal alliance. Member tribes stay self-governing.
institution_arabic_bedouin_clans_desc: Clans bound by blood hold their own oases and trade routes. Wars between tribes are raids for goods that end in reparations; no tribe can absorb another.
institution_arabic_tribal_union_desc: Once enacted, a tribe that wins a war makes the loser acknowledge it as leader (before this, wars end only in reparations), and the winner becomes a tribal alliance. Member tribes stay self-governing.

institution_reform_no_tradition: This culture has no such tradition
institution_arabic_bedouin_clans_desc_in: Clans bound by blood herd and farm the river plains, each under its own chief. Wars between tribes are raids for cattle and goods that end in reparations; no tribe can absorb another.
institution_arabic_tribal_shura_desc_ind: The chieftains raise a king and the alliance becomes a kingdom; royal authority still rests on the clans and the priests.
institution_arabic_caliphal_diwan_desc_i: A council of ministers and its offices keep registers, pay and records, turning oral tribal rule into filed administration.
institution_arabic_caravan_trade_desc_in: Merchants organize in guilds along rivers and ports; tolls and markets become the treasury's mainstay.
institution_arabic_mamluk_corps_desc_ind: Elephants, chariots, horse and foot are kept under arms, loyal to the king who pays them — until a general decides to be king.
institution_arabic_jizya_tax_desc_india: A sixth of every harvest is owed to the king, while village communities keep running their own affairs.
institution_arabic_iqta_military_fiscal_: Village revenues replace salaries for commanders and vassals: the army pays itself, and stops asking the court's permission.
institution_arabic_ulama_jurisprudence_d: Priestly scholars control the law and the courts; the king's decrees must accord with sacred law to be lawful.
institution_arabic_sultanate_bureaucracy: A minister risen from the army holds real power, the king becomes symbolic, and the bureaucracy reorganizes around military merit.
institution_arabic_caliphal_theocracy_de: The king rules as protector of the sacred law: decree and dharma merge, and dissent becomes impiety.
institution_arabic_bayt_al_mal_desc_indi: Tribute, booty and stipends are registered and distributed through a royal treasury, replacing ad hoc tribal division with permanent finance.
institution_arabic_waqf_endowment_desc_i: Land and income are granted in perpetuity to temples for worship, learning and relief, stabilizing social provision while locking revenue into temple property.
institution_arabic_madrasa_network_desc_: Temple wealth supports monastic universities across the realm, teaching scripture, grammar, medicine and mathematics, and supplying trained scholars and officials.
institution_youmu_steppe_clans_desc_azte: Clans farm maize among the lakes and valleys, each under its own chief. Wars between tribes are raids for captives and goods that end in reparations; no tribe can absorb another.
institution_youmu_tribal_confederation_d: The city-states raise a common lord and the alliance becomes a league of cities; it gathers on tribute and scatters on dispute.
institution_youmu_subject_register_desc_: Subjects of every city are enrolled in registers, giving the league a countable tax and manpower base.
institution_youmu_khuriltai_election_des: Royal kin and nobles meet to choose the ruler: succession turns on election and war honours, not birth order.
institution_youmu_decimal_army_desc_azte: Every ward raises its company, dissolving old tribal lines into chains of command.
institution_youmu_steppe_law_desc_aztec: A written code overrides clan custom: the ruler's will finally outranks tradition.
institution_youmu_horse_archer_doctrine_: Warriors rise in rank by the captives they take; elite orders lead the charge and win dominance over neighbouring cities.
institution_youmu_dual_administration_de: Native law governs the home cities and old custom the conquered ones: two parallel administrations that never merge.
institution_youmu_post_relay_network_des: Relay stations and runners span the realm; edicts and intelligence race from post to post.
institution_youmu_provincial_system_desc: Conquered cities are grouped into tributary provinces with resident officials collecting fixed tribute — the league's permanent administration.
institution_youmu_ulus_appanage_desc_azt: Cities, fields and tribute are granted to royal kin in return for loyalty in conquest, giving them a hereditary power base.
institution_youmu_keshig_guard_desc_azte: Sons of the city nobility form the ruler's household guard: an elite army, a school for officials and a network of political hostages.
institution_youmu_steppe_clans_desc_ojib: Clans hunt, fish and gather among the lakes and forests, each under its own chief. Wars between tribes are raids for goods that end in reparations; no tribe can absorb another.
institution_youmu_tribal_confederation_d: The bands kindle a shared council fire and raise a grand chief; the confederacy gathers for war and scatters on dispute.
institution_youmu_subject_register_desc_: Settled subjects are enrolled in registers, giving the confederacy a countable tax and manpower base.
institution_youmu_khuriltai_election_des: Chiefs and elders meet to choose the grand chief: succession turns on acclamation and standing, not birth order.
institution_youmu_decimal_army_desc_ojib: War bands are organized by clan, dissolving old band lines into chains of command.
institution_youmu_steppe_law_desc_ojibwe: A covenant binding all bands overrides local custom: the grand chief's word finally outranks tradition.
institution_youmu_horse_archer_doctrine_: Light raids and forest ambush become doctrine, trading mass for decisive mobility over settled armies.
institution_youmu_dual_administration_de: Band custom governs the people and settled law the farmers: two parallel administrations that never merge.
institution_youmu_post_relay_network_des: Canoe routes link lakes and rivers; commands and news pass from paddler to paddler.
institution_youmu_ulus_appanage_desc_oji: People, hunting grounds and tribute are granted to the grand chief's kin in return for loyalty, giving them a hereditary power base.
institution_youmu_keshig_guard_desc_ojib: Sons of band leaders form the grand chief's guard: an elite force, a school for officials and a network of hostages.

institution_western_principate_desc: Supreme power gathers in a princeps for life while the senate remains only as counsel: the office passes within the princeps' family, and cities taken by the core are no longer all made autonomous city-states but organised into provinces under appointed governors.

caliphal_investiture_history: {0} sends envoys to {1} and is invested by {2} as ruler of {3}.
war_peace_trade: Defeated, {0} is forced to open its ports to {1} for twenty years
institution_western_knighthood_desc: Enfeoffed knights maintain their horses and armour from their fiefs and ride out with their lords in war: the backbone of feudal armies, and a source of confidence for the lords.
institution_western_mercantilism_desc: The state sponsors manufactories and oceanic trade, protects its merchants with tariffs and measures power in bullion; the merchants' voice grows.
institution_western_military_revolution_: Matchlocks and cannon change the battlefield; crown-paid standing infantry and artillery replace knights, and the feudal lords' military edge is gone for good.
institution_western_absolutism_desc: The monarch governs the whole realm directly through a standing army and bureaucracy, revoking the lords' privileges; royal power, in the name of rational reform, is absolute and active.
institution_western_enlightenment_desc: Reason, natural rights and the social contract spread; the rule of law and the separation of powers dominate debate, and the church's authority is questioned: the legal foundation for constitutional rule.
institution_western_abolish_serfdom_desc: Serfs gain personal freedom, land can be bought and sold, and labour flows to towns and workshops; the privileges of lords and landlords crumble.
institution_western_conscription_desc: All adult men are called up in the name of the nation; armies grow far beyond anything before, and war becomes the business of the whole people.
institution_arabic_gunpowder_army_desc: A standing guard under the ruler, armed with matchlocks and cannon, replaces the old slave cavalry; the army answers only to the court.
institution_arabic_gunpowder_army_desc_i: A standing army under the king, armed with matchlocks and cannon, pushes the war elephants into second place; the army answers only to the court.
institution_arabic_iqta_abolition_desc: Tax districts granted to commanders return to the treasury and are replaced with salaries; local warlords lose their own revenue and finance returns to the court.
institution_arabic_iqta_abolition_desc_i: Village revenues granted to commanders and vassals return to the treasury and are replaced with salaries; local vassals lose their own revenue and finance returns to the court.
institution_arabic_reorganization_desc: New laws reorganize offices, penal codes and finance, and all subjects stand equal before the law whatever their faith, laying the administrative and legal groundwork for a constitution.
institution_youmu_sedentarization_desc: The clans gradually settle; pastures and fields are registered together and grain is levied by household, giving the steppe realm stable granaries and a tax base.
institution_youmu_sedentarization_desc_a: Households and fields of every city and village are registered together and grain is levied by household, giving the league stable granaries and a tax base.
institution_youmu_firearms_desc: Battalions trained in muskets and cannon give the realm siege and garrison weapons beyond the mounted archer.
institution_youmu_settled_bureaucracy_de: Examined officials govern the settled subjects, written law replaces tribal custom, and the private powers of princes and nobles give way to the court: the steppe empire's road to a constitution.
institution_huaxia_self_strengthening_de: The court founds arsenals, shipyards and mines under official supervision and merchant management, seeking strength and wealth; modern industry begins.
institution_huaxia_new_army_desc: Drilled by modern manuals and armed with rifled guns, a standing new army takes its officers from military schools while the old battalions are disbanded.
institution_japan_conscription_desc: The warrior class loses its monopoly on arms; every subject may be called up, and conscripts are drafted each year into a standing army.
institution_japan_industrial_promotion_d: The state funds model factories, railways and mines, then sells them to private owners to foster native industry.

relocate_city_description: Click a city's land to select it, then click another stretch of land inside that city's territory (unclaimed land is claimed first): the seat moves there at once, free and instantly, hills are fine, factories and enemy occupation do not matter. The city plan, walls, palace, nameplate, highways and administrative reach are all recalculated around the new site, and villages on the new site merge into the city (clicking one of the city's villages or towns makes it the new seat). The old site remains as a town (a walled town if the city had walls); population, countryside and borders stay as they were. Clicking another city's land switches the selection; a capital stays the capital.

institution_ideology_confucianism_desc_r: The orthodox learning of schools and cloisters: a God-given order of estates, office for the learned, light dues and alms for the poor. Held by clerks and landowners; appears with writing and rites.
institution_ideology_legalism_desc_roma: Students of written law who put the sovereign's law above feudal custom, reclaim lords' courts and levies, discipline officials and strengthen the centre. Held by officials and soldiers; appears with writing and law codes.
institution_ideology_huang_lao_desc_roma: Begging friars who preach poverty, charity and peace, urging rulers to tax less, end wars and feed the hungry. Popular with peasants and townsfolk; appears with writing.
institution_ideology_mohism_desc_roma: Craft guilds of the towns: rules of the trade, skilled work, mutual aid and thrift, lower dues and fair dealing. Held by artisans and townsfolk; appears with writing and masonry.
institution_ideology_agrarianism_desc_ro: Defenders of the village commons and peasant custom against enclosure, seeking lighter rents and labour and land for those who till it. Held by peasants and serfs; appears with writing and census.
institution_ideology_strategists_desc_ro: Self-styled heirs of chivalry who prize valour and honour and seek conquest and fiefs won by the sword. Held by soldiers; appears with writing and muster rolls.
institution_ideology_diplomatists_desc_r: Town merchant leagues and seafarers who value trade, alliances and diplomacy backed by silver. Held by merchants and wandering scholars; appears with writing and coinage.
institution_ideology_yin_yang_desc_roma: Put the Church above the crown: an established faith, kingship sanctioned by God and clergy in government. Held by the clergy; appears with rites.
institution_ideology_imperial_power_desc: Crown above vassals: curb the great lords and gather power to the throne. Held by the royal household and clerks; at court, the Royalists.
institution_ideology_great_clans_desc_ro: Hereditary lords who prize blood and fiefs and want grants, privileges and the right to wage their own wars. Held by the nobility; at court, the Barons.
institution_ideology_consort_kin_desc_ro: The queen's family, raised by marriage, meddling in government and the succession. Only at court, as the Queen's Party.
faction_represents_RoyalKin_roma: for the princes of the blood
institution_ideology_royal_kin_desc_roma: Princes of the ruler's own blood seeking appanages, upkeep and inheritance. Only at court, as the Princes' Party.
institution_ideology_military_merit_desc: Commanders and military officers who rose by war and favour campaigns, expansion and unification. Only at court, as the Marshals.
institution_ideology_confucianism_desc_a: Scholars of sacred law who teach scripture and justice: office for the learned, light taxes, care for the poor and lawful order. Held by learned officials and landowners; appears with writing and rites.
institution_ideology_legalism_desc_arabi: Would have the sovereign's decrees complete the sacred law, reclaim provincial troops and revenues, discipline officials and strengthen the centre. Held by officials and soldiers; appears with writing and law codes.
institution_ideology_huang_lao_desc_arab: Mystics of inner devotion and love who live simply and urge rulers to mercy, light taxes and peace. Popular with peasants and townsfolk; appears with writing.
institution_ideology_mohism_desc_arabic: Craft guilds and brotherhoods of the towns: rules of the trade, mutual aid and skill, lower taxes and fairness. Held by artisans and townsfolk; appears with writing and masonry.
institution_ideology_agrarianism_desc_ar: Guardians of villages and irrigation channels against land-grabbing magnates, seeking lower rents and taxes and land for those who till it. Held by peasants; appears with writing and census.
institution_ideology_strategists_desc_ar: Frontier warriors who glory in fighting for the faith and seek conquest and grants won in war. Held by soldiers; appears with writing and muster rolls.
institution_ideology_diplomatists_desc_a: Caravan and sea merchants of the trade routes who value commerce, alliances and diplomacy backed by wealth. Held by merchants and wandering scholars; appears with writing and coinage.
institution_ideology_yin_yang_desc_arabi: Court astrologers who read the fate of the realm in the stars, proclaim kingship ordained by heaven and urge honour to the faith and its holy places. Held by clerics and diviners; appears with rites.
institution_ideology_imperial_power_desc: The sovereign above all, relying on courtiers, slave soldiers and eunuchs to curb provincial magnates. At court, the Sovereign's Party.
institution_ideology_great_clans_desc_ar: Tribal chiefs and great landowners who prize lineage and privilege and want grants, rights and their own armies. Held by nobles; at court, the Notables.
faction_represents_ConsortKin_arabic: for the harem & the queen mother's kin
institution_ideology_consort_kin_desc_ar: Consorts of the harem and the queen mother's kin, using the palace to sway government and the succession. Only at court, as the Harem Party.
institution_ideology_eunuchs_desc_arabic: Palace eunuchs who serve the ruler and guard the palace and harem, normally siding with the Sovereign's Party; under a weak ruler they form their own faction and seize power. Only at court.
institution_ideology_royal_kin_desc_arab: Princes of the ruler's own blood seeking lands, upkeep and a claim to the throne. Only at court, as the Princes' Party.
institution_ideology_military_merit_desc: Commanders and military officers who rose by war and favour campaigns, expansion and unification. Only at court, as the Commanders.
institution_ideology_confucianism_desc_i: The ancient law books: everyone keeping their station and the king upholding the law, office for the learned, light taxes and the order of rites. Held by learned officials and landowners; appears with writing and rites.
institution_ideology_legalism_desc_india: The science of rule and gain: strict rewards and punishments, spies everywhere, vassal armies brought under the crown. Held by officials and soldiers; appears with writing and law codes.
institution_ideology_huang_lao_desc_indi: Wandering renunciants who preach non-violence and purity, urging mild punishments, light taxes and peace. Popular with peasants and townsfolk; appears with writing.
institution_ideology_mohism_desc_india: Craft and trade guilds with their own rules, mutual aid and thrift, skill and fair dealing, seeking lower taxes. Held by artisans and townsfolk; appears with writing and masonry.
institution_ideology_agrarianism_desc_in: Guardians of village councils and irrigated fields against land-grabbing magnates, seeking lower rents and taxes. Held by peasants; appears with writing and census.
institution_ideology_strategists_desc_in: Champions of the warrior's duty who prize valour and honour and seek conquest and rewards won in war. Held by soldiers; appears with writing and muster rolls.
institution_ideology_diplomatists_desc_i: Merchants of the sea lanes and caravan roads who value trade, alliances and diplomacy backed by wealth. Held by merchants and wandering scholars; appears with writing and coinage.
institution_ideology_yin_yang_desc_india: Priests of the sacrifice who teach the will of the gods and the rites, proclaim divine kingship and seek honour for priests and an established faith. Held by priests; appears with rites.
institution_ideology_imperial_power_desc: The king above all, relying on ministers and scribes to curb the vassals. At court, the Royalists.
institution_ideology_great_clans_desc_in: Hereditary nobles and great landowners who prize lineage and privilege and want grants, rights and their own armies. Held by nobles; at court, the Nobles.
institution_ideology_consort_kin_desc_in: The queen's family, raised by marriage, meddling in government and the succession. Only at court, as the Queen's Party.
institution_ideology_royal_kin_desc_indi: Princes of the ruler's own blood seeking lands, upkeep and a claim to the throne. Only at court, as the Princes' Party.
institution_ideology_military_merit_desc: Commanders and military officers who rose by war and favour campaigns, expansion and unification. Only at court, as the Marshals.
institution_ideology_confucianism_desc_y: Keepers of the forefathers' customs and the ranks of the clans: office for the able, light levies and relief for the people. Held by officials and herd-owners; appears with writing and rites.
institution_ideology_legalism_desc_youmu: Would rule the clans by the khan's written law, with strict rewards and punishments, the princes' troops reclaimed and the khan strengthened. Held by officials and soldiers; appears with writing and law codes.
institution_ideology_huang_lao_desc_youm: Let the herders follow the grass in peace: fewer levies, fewer wars and lenient rule. Popular with herders and commoners; appears with writing.
institution_ideology_mohism_desc_youmu: Craftsmen who follow the camps, valuing tools and building, thrift and mutual aid, and seeking lighter levies. Held by artisans; appears with writing and masonry.
institution_ideology_agrarianism_desc_yo: Herding is the root: guard the common pastures against the nobles' fences and lighten the tribute. Held by herders and subject folk; appears with writing and census.
institution_ideology_strategists_desc_yo: The realm stands on horse and bow: prize valour, ride to conquest and be rewarded for victories. Held by soldiers; appears with writing and muster rolls.
institution_ideology_diplomatists_desc_y: Caravan masters and interpreters of the trade roads who value markets, marriage alliances and diplomacy. Held by merchants and wandering scholars; appears with writing and coinage.
institution_ideology_yin_yang_desc_youmu: Shamans who speak with the spirits and the sky, proclaim heaven's mandate for the khan and seek sky worship as the state faith. Held by shamans; appears with rites.
institution_ideology_imperial_power_desc: The khan above all, relying on his household and guards to curb the clan chiefs. At court, the Khan's Party.
institution_ideology_great_clans_desc_yo: Clan chiefs and nobles who prize blood and followers and want grants, privileges and their own warbands. Held by nobles; at court, the Nobles.
faction_represents_ConsortKin_youmu: for the clans married into the khan's house
institution_ideology_consort_kin_desc_yo: Clans that marry into the khan's house, using the bond to sway government and the succession. Only at court, as the Consort Party.
faction_represents_RoyalKin_youmu: for the princes of the khan's house
institution_ideology_royal_kin_desc_youm: Princes of the khan's house seeking lands, people and a claim to the throne. Only at court, as the Princes' Party.
institution_ideology_military_merit_desc: Commanders and military officers who rose by war and favour campaigns, expansion and unification. Only at court, as the Military Merit Faction.
institution_ideology_confucianism_desc_a: Keepers of the elders' teachings and the order of ranks, schooling noble youth, giving office to the able and relief to the poor. Held by officials and landowners; appears with writing and rites.
institution_ideology_legalism_desc_aztec: Would rule the cities by the king's laws, with strict rewards and punishments, subject cities disarmed and the crown strengthened. Held by officials and soldiers; appears with writing and law codes.
institution_ideology_huang_lao_desc_azte: Urge the king to ask less tribute and wage fewer wars, and to deal gently with the common folk. Popular with peasants and townsfolk; appears with writing.
institution_ideology_mohism_desc_aztec: Featherworkers, goldsmiths and other craftsmen bound in societies, valuing skill, mutual aid and thrift and seeking lighter tribute. Held by artisans and townsfolk; appears with writing and masonry.
institution_ideology_agrarianism_desc_az: Guardians of the wards' shared fields and floating gardens against noble land-grabbing, seeking lighter tribute. Held by peasants and subject folk; appears with writing and census.
institution_ideology_strategists_desc_az: Eagle and jaguar warriors who win glory by taking captives and seek wars on every side and tribute from the subdued. Held by soldiers; appears with writing and muster rolls.
institution_ideology_diplomatists_desc_a: Far-travelling merchants who double as spies, valuing trade, alliances and diplomacy backed by goods and news. Held by merchants; appears with writing and coinage.
institution_ideology_yin_yang_desc_aztec: Temple priests who keep the calendar and the offerings, read the will of the gods and proclaim divine kingship with the temples as the root of the realm. Held by priests; appears with rites.
institution_ideology_imperial_power_desc: The king above all, relying on ministers and scribes to curb the lords of subject cities. At court, the Royalists.
institution_ideology_great_clans_desc_az: Hereditary nobles who prize lineage and privilege and want grants, rights and their own warriors. Held by nobles; at court, the Nobles.
institution_ideology_consort_kin_desc_az: The queen's family, raised by marriage, meddling in government and the succession. Only at court, as the Queen's Party.
institution_ideology_royal_kin_desc_azte: Princes of the ruler's own blood seeking lands, upkeep and a claim to the throne. Only at court, as the Princes' Party.
institution_ideology_military_merit_desc: Warrior chiefs and commanders who rose by war and favour campaigns, expansion and unification. Only at court, as the Marshals.
institution_ideology_confucianism_desc_o: Honour the elders and clan customs, choose leaders by virtue and standing, care for the needy and keep the proper order. Held by elders and headmen; appears with writing and rites.
institution_ideology_huang_lao_desc_ojib: Decide everything in council around the fire by common consent; fewer wars and lenient dealings with all peoples. Popular with the people; appears with writing.
institution_ideology_agrarianism_desc_oj: Forests, hunting grounds and rice lakes belong to all; no headman may take them for himself, and levies should be light. Held by the people; appears with writing and census.
institution_ideology_strategists_desc_oj: Warrior societies who prize war honours and a brave name and seek raids of revenge and wider hunting grounds. Held by warriors; appears with writing and muster rolls.
institution_ideology_diplomatists_desc_o: Traders of the lakes and rivers who value gift exchange, alliances and commerce. Held by traders; appears with writing and coinage.
institution_ideology_yin_yang_desc_ojibw: Healers of the medicine society who speak with the spirits and cure the sick, seeking honour for their order and the spirits' will in great matters. Held by shamans; appears with rites.
institution_ideology_imperial_power_desc: Raise the head chief above the clan headmen so that one voice commands. Held by the head chief's confidants; at court, the Chief's Party.
institution_ideology_great_clans_desc_oj: Clan headmen who prize clan autonomy and inheritance and want land, rights and their own war parties. Held by headmen; at court, the Headmen.
institution_ideology_military_merit_desc: War chiefs and leading warriors who made their names in battle and favour war, wider hunting grounds and uniting the peoples. Only at court, as the War Chiefs.
institution_ideology_confucianism_desc_j: Rites, righteousness and proper station; rule by virtue and education and the order of lord and vassal. Held by officials and landowners; appears with writing and rites.
institution_ideology_legalism_desc_japan: Govern by the law codes, take back the great houses' private lands and soldiers, discipline officials and strengthen the court. Held by officials and soldiers; appears with writing and law codes.
institution_ideology_huang_lao_desc_japa: Teach compassion and karma, urging rulers to mild punishments, light taxes, peace and famine relief. Popular with peasants and townsfolk; appears with writing.
institution_ideology_mohism_desc_japan: Craftsmen of every trade in their guilds, valuing skill, rules of the trade, mutual aid and thrift and seeking lower taxes. Held by artisans and townsfolk; appears with writing and masonry.
institution_ideology_agrarianism_desc_ja: Farming is the root of the realm: protect villages and fields from the grasping great houses and lower the yearly tax. Held by peasants; appears with writing and census.
institution_ideology_strategists_desc_ja: Students of strategy and the way of bow and horse who prize valour and honour and seek glory in war. Held by soldiers; appears with writing and muster rolls.
institution_ideology_diplomatists_desc_j: Merchants and envoys of the sea lanes who value trade, markets and negotiation. Held by merchants and wandering scholars; appears with writing and coinage.
institution_ideology_yin_yang_desc_japan: Worship of the gods of heaven and earth and the ancestors: the ruler descends from the gods, rites and rule are one, and shrines should be honoured. Held by shrine priests; appears with rites.
institution_ideology_great_clans_desc_ja: Great houses and court nobles of long lineage who prize rank and privilege and share rule with the throne. Held by nobles; at court, the Great Houses.
institution_ideology_royal_kin_desc_japa: Princes of the imperial blood seeking estates, upkeep and a claim to the throne. Only at court, as the Princes' Party.
institution_ideology_military_merit_desc: Warrior houses and commanders who rose by war and favour campaigns, expansion and unification. Only at court, as the Warrior Houses.
institution_ideology_yin_yang_desc_perse: Keepers of the sacred fire who preach the struggle of good and evil and the king's divine glory, urging divine kingship and the fire faith as state religion. Held by priests; appears with rites.
institution_ideology_yin_yang_desc_egypt: Temple priests who keep rites and the calendar, hail the ruler as a child of the gods and seek rich endowments and an established faith. Held by priests; appears with rites.
institution_ideology_confucianism_desc_v: The law of the forefathers and the customs of the assembly: the worthy take counsel, dues stay light and neighbours are helped. Held by lawspeakers and landowners; appears with writing and rites.
institution_ideology_strategists_desc_vi: Warbands who follow their chief over the sea, glorying in plunder and deeds and seeking new lands and tribute. Held by warriors; appears with writing and muster rolls.
institution_ideology_yin_yang_desc_vikin: Priests of the old gods who read fate and the will of the gods, proclaim the chief favoured by heaven and seek honour for the sacrifices. Held by priests; appears with rites.
institution_ideology_confucianism_desc_k: Sages of the law and the scriptures who teach covenant and justice, office for the learned and care for the poor. Held by learned officials and landowners; appears with writing and rites.
institution_ideology_yin_yang_desc_koshe: Temple priests of sacrifice and purity who proclaim kingship ordained by God and seek honour for the temple. Held by priests; appears with rites.

institution_zhou_enfeoffment_desc: Land is parcelled out to kin and retainers who hold full military and civil power in their fiefs.
institution_huaxia_tributary_system_desc: The Son of Heaven at the centre, the four quarters submitting: neighbours send envoys and tribute in return for investiture and trade. Required before accepting tributaries or waging tribute wars.
institution_zhou_forbid_private_wars_des: Lords may no longer wage war on their own; the right of conquest reverts to the crown.
institution_zhou_reduce_vassals_desc: Fiefs are dismantled into commanderies run by appointed officials instead of hereditary lords. If the vassals already hold their fiefs by hereditary right, this becomes an abolition of the domains, with far greater resistance and risk of rebellion.
institution_youmu_tribal_confederation_d: The clans raise a great khan and the alliance becomes a khanate under nomadic rule; it gathers on plunder and scatters on dispute.
institution_youmu_subject_register_desc: Settled subjects are enrolled in registers, giving the steppe realm a countable tax and manpower base.
institution_youmu_provincial_tax_farming: Tax districts are auctioned to merchant collectors: nomadic regimes collect 75% of the usual tax instead of 50% (tax level still limited to None or Low), and the provinces are squeezed raw.
institution_youmu_dual_administration_de: Steppe law governs the nomads and settled law the farmers: two parallel bureaucracies that never merge.
institution_culture_ranking_hint: Tiers use the highest advancement in each branch. Lowering one manually causes institutional regression and angers groups that lose established benefits.
institution_western_classical_city_repub: Assemblies and elected magistrates run the city: power is term-limited, collegial and checked.
institution_western_feudalization_desc: Offices become fiefs and fiefs become heritable: public authority fragments into layers of private homage.
institution_western_feudal_contract_desc: Homage runs both ways: the lord must respect chartered privileges, and breach entitles vassals to defy him.
institution_western_secular_estates_desc: Estates trade tax consent for a legislative voice, and secular orders begin to outweigh the church.
institution_western_centralized_monarchy: Standing armies, crown tax collectors and royal courts replace feudal middlemen: the king reaches every subject.
institution_western_clerical_supremacy_d: The church controls investiture, schooling and conscience; secular rulers must bow to it.
institution_western_theocratic_state_des: Crown and altar merge: the ruler governs by divine mandate and the clerical hierarchy is the civil service.
institution_arabic_tribal_shura_desc: The chieftains deliberate and acclaim a successor, and the alliance becomes a caliphate under Arabic rule; authority still rests on clan consent.
institution_arabic_caliphal_diwan_desc: Registries of people, pay and correspondence turn oral rule into filed administration.
institution_arabic_iqta_military_fiscal_: Tax districts replace salaries for commanders: the army pays itself, and stops asking the court's permission.
institution_arabic_sultanate_bureaucracy: A soldier-sultan holds real power, the caliph becomes symbolic, and the bureaucracy reorganizes around military merit.
institution_arabic_ulama_jurisprudence_d: Jurists control interpretation and the courts; the ruler's decrees need their sanction to be lawful.
institution_arabic_caliphal_theocracy_de: The sovereign heads the faith itself: decree and doctrine merge, and dissent becomes heresy.
institution_huaxia_prefecture_county_bur: The realm becomes uniform prefectures and counties run by assessed, rotated officials — rule by paperwork, not blood. Reached either by abolishing the fiefs outright or gradually through the Grace Edict.
institution_huaxia_examination_officiald: Office is won by written examination, opening the bureaucracy to commoners and narrowing hereditary privilege. Great-clan sons no longer have priority for vacancies. Replaces the Recommendation System and the Nine-Rank System.
institution_huaxia_warlord_succession_de: Regional garrison commanders grow powerful enough to decide succession by force, unlocking the Rule of the Strongest succession law.
institution_huaxia_tactical_drilling_des: Standardized drill formations and battlefield doctrine improve every soldier's combat performance.
institution_huaxia_primitive_band_desc: Hunter-gatherer bands know their mothers but not their fathers; people bear only given names and no surnames. Clans with surnames form only once settled villages appear.
institution_huaxia_matrilineal_clan_desc: Settled matrilineal clans now have surnames. Children join their mother's clan and take her surname; clans bear ancient names such as Ji, Jiang, Si and Ying.
institution_huaxia_patrilineal_clan_desc: Copper tools and the plough make men the main producers; descent is now traced through the father and clans begin to divide into rich and poor. Nobles branch new lineage names (shi) off their surname: from fiefs, towns or ancestors.
institution_huaxia_tribal_alliance_desc: Rammed-earth towns rise and tribes learn to join by war and pact: once enacted, a tribe that wins a war makes the loser acknowledge it as common lord (before this, wars end only in reparations), and the winner becomes a tribal alliance. The common lord is chosen for merit and abdicates to a successor (Yao, Shun, Yu). Member tribes stay self-governing.
institution_huaxia_hereditary_kingship_d: Bronze cauldrons are cast and abdication ends: the throne passes from father to son (Xia, Shang). Beyond the royal domain lie many vassal polities bound by ritual and war.
institution_huaxia_patriarchal_clan_desc: Rule rests on kinship and ritual: the sovereign heads the senior lineage. Under patriarchal custom, automatic appointments and faction leadership favor men. Men are called by their shi and women by their surname; commoners have neither and use only given names, until surname and shi merge under the commandery system.
institution_huaxia_well_field_desc: Fields are divided into public and private plots; households farm the common plot in lieu of tax.
institution_huaxia_land_equalization_des: Land and levies are assigned per registered adult, moving the tax base from lords to the state census. The state allots land per adult and restricts its accumulation. On completion, land annexation (a court malady) eases by 30.
institution_huaxia_salt_iron_monopoly_de: Salt, iron and liquor become state monopolies, doubling revenue without new taxes — and angering merchants.
institution_huaxia_military_garrison_des: Soldier-farmers serve in rotation from state garrisons, cutting costs and ending reliance on lords' retainers.
institution_arabic_caravan_trade_desc: Camel caravans link desert routes; tolls and markets become the treasury's mainstay.
institution_arabic_mamluk_corps_desc: Slave-soldiers form a standing elite loyal only to whoever pays them — until they decide to rule themselves.
institution_arabic_jizya_tax_desc: A per-head tax on non-adherents buys them autonomy and exemption from service.
institution_western_civic_legion_desc: Propertied citizens arm themselves and fight in formation; service and franchise reinforce each other.
institution_western_roman_law_desc: Codified statute plus juristic commentary gives contract, property and litigation rules that can be cited.
institution_western_manorial_economy_des: Self-sufficient manors bind serfs to the lord's land and the lord's court.
institution_western_burgher_charters_des: Towns buy charters of self-rule; guilds and councils carve an enclave out of feudal jurisdiction.
institution_youmu_khuriltai_election_des: Princes and nobles convene to raise a khan: succession turns on acclamation and strength, not birth order.
institution_youmu_decimal_army_desc: The whole people is organized in tens, hundreds and thousands, dissolving old tribal lines into chains of command.
institution_youmu_steppe_law_desc: A written khanal code overrides tribal custom: the khan's will finally outranks tradition.
institution_youmu_horse_archer_doctrine_: Light horse archery and feigned retreat become doctrine, trading mass for decisive mobility over settled armies.
institution_youmu_post_relay_network_des: Relay stations span the realm; edicts and intelligence travel at the speed of fresh horses.
institution_youmu_provincial_system_desc: Branch secretariats administer conquered farmland through a permanent provincial hierarchy — the steppe empire's answer to settling down.

bakufu_established_history: {0} opens a shogunate: {1} becomes shōgun and rules, while Emperor {2} reigns in name
institution_japan_land_tax_reform_desc: A fixed tax on assessed land value founds modern state finance.
institution_japan_meiji_restoration_desc: Power returns to the emperor, domains become prefectures, all commoners take family names and the country opens.
institution_japan_sakoku_desc: Christianity is banned and foreign trade confined to Nagasaki; foreign ideas cannot reach a closed country.
institution_japan_sankin_kotai_desc: Daimyō alternate years in Edo and leave their families as hostages.
institution_japan_bakufu_desc: The shōgun opens a shogunate and holds real power while the emperor reigns in Kyoto; daimyō hold hereditary domains.
institution_japan_shoen_estates_desc: Public land flows into tax-exempt noble and temple estates.
institution_japan_samurai_bands_desc: Provincial warriors band together; samurai take their land as their family name (myōji).
institution_japan_sekkan_regency_desc: The Fujiwara in-laws rule as regents while the emperor reigns in name.
institution_japan_handen_desc: Households are registered and fields allotted per person in return for taxes.
institution_japan_ritsuryo_state_desc: The Taika Reform copies Tang law codes: the emperor rules through the Council of State, and provinces are governed by kokushi.
institution_japan_kabane_ranks_desc: Emperor Tenmu ranks the noble clans with eight hereditary titles.
institution_japan_yamato_kingship_desc: The great king unites the clans under the uji-kabane system: nobles bear clan names and ranks, commoners have none.
institution_japan_yayoi_kuni_desc: Rice farming and bronze arrive from the continent; a hundred small kingdoms follow Queen Himiko of Yamatai. Still no surnames.
institution_japan_jomon_tribes_desc: Hunter-gatherer settlements making cord-marked pottery. People bear only given names.

institution_huaxia_two_tax_law_desc: Levies shift from personal labor obligations to twice-yearly assessments of land and property, moving the tax base from bodies to wealth. Replaces the Equal-Field system. On completion, land annexation and exorbitant levies each ease by 20.
institution_huaxia_single_whip_reform_de: Land tax, labor service and miscellaneous levies are consolidated into a single silver payment, simplifying accounts while forcing households into the cash economy. On completion, a land survey eases land annexation by 30, exorbitant levies by 25 and corrupt officials by 10.
institution_huaxia_abolish_well_field_de: The well-field system is abolished: private fields are recognized, taxed by area, and may be bought and sold. Feudal regimes have no landlord class, so the land market only truly functions after the switch to the Code-and-Statute regime.
institution_huaxia_merit_ranks_desc: Ranks are granted for battlefield merit, letting commoners rise into the nobility and ending the hereditary lords' monopoly on arms.
institution_huaxia_recommendation_desc: Local officials recommend the filial and talented for office, giving the court control of appointments — though family standing and favoritism creep in.
institution_huaxia_constitutional_prepar: Constitutional government is prepared: provinces seat consultative assemblies and the court an advisory council where gentry and merchants debate state affairs. This is Huaxia's administrative basis for constitutional monarchy; requires the Prefecture-County Bureaucracy and the Single Whip Reform.
institution_resistance_reason_constituti: Gentry and merchants debating policy in the assemblies erodes absolute rule by the throne and its officials
institution_huaxia_recruited_army_desc: A treasury-funded professional army replaces rotating militia service, improving reliability while increasing military costs and commanders' influence.
institution_western_great_charter_desc: The ruler accepts written limits on taxation, justice and the punishment of vassals, turning feudal custom into enforceable political privilege.
institution_western_parliamentary_taxati: The estates trade tax consent for deliberation and oversight, converting urban wealth into durable political representation.
institution_western_reformation_desc: Local churches and secular rulers challenge universal clerical authority, redrawing the boundaries of faith, church property and political loyalty.
institution_arabic_bayt_al_mal_desc: Tribute, booty and stipends are registered and distributed through a central treasury, replacing ad hoc tribal division with permanent finance.
institution_arabic_waqf_endowment_desc: Land and income are permanently endowed for worship, education and relief, stabilizing social provision while locking revenue into religious property.
institution_arabic_madrasa_network_desc: Endowments support colleges across the realm, standardizing legal education and supplying trained jurists and administrators.
institution_youmu_ulus_appanage_desc: People, pasture and revenue are granted to royal princes in return for loyalty in conquest, giving those princes a hereditary power base.
institution_youmu_keshig_guard_desc: Sons of tribal nobles form the khan's household guard: an elite army, a school for officials and a network of political hostages.
institution_youmu_religious_tolerance_de: Conquered peoples keep their faith and clergy, trading religious autonomy for taxes, expertise and imperial loyalty.

institution_ideology_anarchism_desc: Abolish coercive state power in favour of voluntary, self-governing communes. Once unlocked, parties of this ideology may form in this culture.
institution_ideology_social_democracy_de: Gradual reform through parliament: welfare and labour protection narrow the gap between rich and poor. Once unlocked, parties of this ideology may form in this culture.
institution_ideology_libertarianism_desc: Individual liberty above all: the smallest possible government, with markets and contracts ordering society. Once unlocked, parties of this ideology may form in this culture.
institution_ideology_social_liberalism_d: Civil rights and equal opportunity, with measured state action to correct market injustice. Once unlocked, parties of this ideology may form in this culture.
institution_ideology_capitalism_desc: Private property and free markets are the root of prosperity; commerce and industry lead the economy. Once unlocked, parties of this ideology may form in this culture.

parliament_how_body:
[Seats] Parliament has {0} seats, divided among factions by central share using the largest-remainder method. Banned factions get no seats.
[Members] Each faction sends its own adult members, ranked by: holding office first, then performance, then renown. The emperor cannot sit in parliament. Seats a faction cannot fill stay vacant.
[Term] A general election is held every {1} years. When a member dies, leaves the empire or changes faction, their faction fills the seat in a by-election.
[Powers] Taxes cannot change unless pro-constitution members hold a majority. The emperor still reigns by succession law, no powerful minister arises while parliament sits, and the old cabinet is dissolved.
parliament_responsible_government_body: [Responsible government] Only the government side can start and advance faction claims. In a majority or minority government that is the PM's faction; in a coalition government it is every pro-constitution faction in the coalition. Claims advance faster when the government holds a majority.

parliament_politics_body:
[Seats] Set by the order of magnitude of the population: 9 seats at 100 people, plus 6 for every tenfold increase (21 at 10,000, 33 at 1 million), up to 45. Takes effect at the next election.
[Forming a government] A party with a majority governs alone. Otherwise the largest party (then the second largest) courts the parties closest to it in ideology until it has a majority, forming a coalition; parties too far apart will not join. If talks fail, a minority government is formed.
[Cabinet] Under responsible government, ministries are divided among the governing parties by their seats, and each party picks its own ministers.
[No confidence] A minority government, rifts in the coalition, ministers accused of crimes, public unrest and an empty treasury all invite the opposition to call a vote of no confidence. If it passes, a new majority coalition takes over if one can be formed; otherwise parliament is dissolved for an early election.
[Agenda] The governing party pushes to change one constitutional clause at a time and needs enough votes to amend the constitution; without them it stalls at the second reading. After a change of government, the new government keeps the agenda if it agrees, otherwise drops it.

local_politics_help_body:
In electoral states (parties legal, a parliament, multiple parties), each province has its own party support based on its own voters. Halfway through each parliamentary term, local elections are held: the party with the most votes governs the province and one of its local members becomes governor.
Provinces governed by the coalition get +3 city loyalty. Provinces held by the opposition resist the center: -5 city loyalty, and the government agenda slows in proportion to the population they control (up to 40% slower).
If the opposition holds over 60% of the provinces in two local elections in a row, a unitary state is forced to amend its constitution and become federal. The capital province is run directly by the center and holds no local elections.

empirecraft_law_no_commoners_description: Each month, surplus ordinary residents are folded into population data (head counts grouped by class, culture and ideology). Only notable people (rulers, city lords, officials, nobles, landlords, party members) stay as units, cutting unit counts for much higher frame rates. When an office or city lordship is vacant, someone is raised from the population on the spot, so the total population stays the same. Production and construction are settled automatically from population data. Armies work like CK3 levies: in peacetime each city keeps a single general; when war breaks out, soldiers are raised on the spot from the population up to the city's troop limit and disbanded back into it when the war ends. Folded population grows through births and deaths: more food surplus means more births, prosperity lowers deaths but also birth rates, and famine and war raise deaths. How many people a city holds depends on its houses and other buildings. The population also produces by employment: peasants grow food, workers earn gold and speed up construction, merchants and citizens earn gold, and everyone eats one food per year. Turning this off freezes the folded population; it does not turn back into units.
